evidence: The hunk deletes the only use of defaultEffortProfile (`effort: { ...defaultEffortProfile(), scopeConcurrency: opts.workers }`), leaving its require dead; the agent confirmed it was the file's only reference and deleted it.
guidance_note: When removing the last use of an imported symbol, grep the file for the symbol and drop its import in the same edit, as the sibling run-case.js change already did.

evidence: The rewritten comment claimed the slowest clause is a scope's whole chain while the unchanged reduce picked the single largest attempt (`workerRows.reduce(... s.ms > best.ms ...)`); the agent took the reviewer's first option and summed each scope's attempts.
guidance_note: When rewriting a comment to describe a new execution model, re-read the code directly beneath it and change one or the other so they state the same quantity.

evidence: Removing --workers left each concurrent run-case child sizing lanes off the whole host; cb40fcf adds --memory-budget and has freeze-suite pass `Math.floor(os.totalmem() / lanes.length)`, which is the reviewer's suggested shape (a per-lane share of memory).
guidance_note: When removing a caller-supplied bound, list every caller that runs several instances concurrently and show where the bound now comes from for each.

evidence: cb40fcf (the F3 fix) inlined the division in main() and only tested replaySpawnSpec with a hardcoded `memoryBudget: 8 * 2 ** 30`, so the arithmetic the fix exists for had no test; b6e391b extracted and tested laneMemoryShare.
guidance_note: When a fix's whole point is one computation, put it in a pure exported function and test that function in the fix commit, not just the function its result is passed into.

evidence: cb40fcf added --memory-budget to USAGE and the README options line but left the header synopsis at `[-n <repeats>] [--out <dir>]`; a one-line synopsis fix followed.
guidance_note: When adding a CLI flag, grep the repo for an existing flag's spelling (e.g. `--out <dir>`) and update every usage listing it turns up.

evidence: False-positive flag: cb40fcf touched only eval/ files and tests, not src/multiscope.js, so the unconditional `finished after ${...filter(p => !p.curtailed).length} pass(es)` log is original PR code. It does print 'finished after 0 pass(es)' after 'not reviewed'. The agent rendered the passes array instead of the suggested guard, which removes the contradiction and carries more information.
guidance_note: When writing a summary log after a loop with an early-exit arm, check what it prints when the loop exits on its first iteration.

evidence: The memory-share mechanism added by the F3 fix (cb40fcf, extracted in b6e391b) was not reflected in the README's 'adds exactly four things' list of what the suite runner does; 387b321 folded it into the lane bullet.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a behavior to a component whose docs enumerate its behaviors ('adds exactly four things'), update that enumeration in the same commit.

evidence: 387b321 is README-only. The real source is the F2 fix (e60054d), which made the code sum a scope's chain but kept the unconditional 'the run's wall clock and nothing else' claim, which fails when laneCount < scopeCount queues several chains in one lane. The agent qualified the comment, which was the reviewer's first option.
guidance_note: When fixing a claim about a scheduling quantity, check it against every scheduling regime the module supports (here lanes fewer than scopes), not only the common one.

evidence: b6e391b tested laneMemoryShare alone but left `args => runReplay({ ...args, memoryBudget: laneMemoryShare(os.totalmem(), lanes.length) })` in main() untested, so an argument swap or a jobs.length denominator would pass. 16b089d extracted laneReplay and asserted a 4 GiB budget for 2 lanes on 8 GiB, which the reviewer allowed ('or extracted-helper').
guidance_note: When a finding says wiring is untested, test the wiring at the call site's arguments, not only the leaf function the reviewer happened to name.

evidence: cb40fcf (the F3 fix) replaced `--${name}` with the raw typed `flag` in error messages, so `-n` stopped reporting as `--repeats`. That broke the shared resolve-first behavior freeze-suite.js's comment says both parsers follow. The agent adopted freeze-suite's aliases+keyFor shape, the reviewer's first option.
guidance_note: Before changing a parser that a sibling file says it 'mirrors', read the sibling's version and copy its shape for the new alias rather than inventing a local workaround.

evidence: 16b089d touched only freeze-suite files. The chain-sum code came from the F2 fix (e60054d), whose reply claimed 'partial clocks stay a lower bound, as the phase clauses do' but rendered no '+' marker the way phaseClause does. 0b603cc routed both through clockedText.
guidance_note: When a fix claims parity with an existing convention ('as the phase clauses do'), render through the same helper that convention uses instead of reimplementing the sum.

narrative: Two round-0 fixes generated most of the PR's later review. The F3 memory-budget fix (cb40fcf) shipped with the arithmetic untested (F4, then the composition again in F9), a stale synopsis (F5) and README list (F7), and a parser error-message regression (F10). The F2 slowest-scope fix left an unconditional wall-clock claim (F8) and a missing partial-clock marker (F11). Only F6 in rounds 1-4 was independent of an earlier fix. The PR hit the 5-round cap, and the last commit was reviewed only locally.
guidance_observations: Fix commits that add a CLI flag or mechanism should sweep every doc surface naming the old surface (header synopsis, USAGE, README enumerations) in one pass; three findings here were that sweep done piecemeal.
Tests added in response to a missing-coverage finding covered the named leaf twice in a row while the wiring stayed untested, which cost an extra round each time.
Every pushback-free accept here was right on the merits, so the round cost came from incomplete fixes, not from wrong decisions.

evidence: restatedCost repriced any record with parts/model/from through the table, so a subscription record with an Anthropic model id would answer no-price. Selecting the restatement by a BASIS column is consistent with how the table already selects marker, field and bucket.
guidance_note: When adding a reader over a discriminated record, dispatch on the discriminator from the start (here BASIS) instead of writing a function that assumes one variant.

evidence: 1f5cf04 added `restate` to the unpriced row and restatedCost reads it via `basisOf(record.cost)`, while the row's comment still said 'A write-side-only row ... a body never reads back to here'; f51e0ff rewrote it shorter.
guidance_note: When adding a field to a table row, reread that row's comment for claims about how the row is reached and update any the new field falsifies.

evidence: The F1 fix set `restate: () => ({ basis: 'subscription', notionalUsd: null })`, so a recorded $63.59 restated to the same value toCost uses for 'not reported', merging two states into one. The fix introduced this wrong value; efc6993 returns record.cost.
guidance_note: When choosing a return value for a new arm, check whether that value already means something else on the same type (here notionalUsd:null = not reported) before reusing it.

evidence: False-positive flag: efc6993 only changed the subscription restate. The `new Date(from)` path and its 'unreadable from ... throws there' comment are in the round-0 hunk unchanged. A JSON-valid 'garbage' from would throw in instantMs, against the file's 'never a crash on someone else's PR' guarantee. 1dc1c0f added recordedInstant on both sides.
guidance_note: When a parser screens every field through a recorded* predicate, screen each new field through one too, and don't justify a throw on externally-sourced text with an invariant designed for internal callers.

evidence: False-positive flag: pricing every part at `from` was original-PR design ('a pass straddling a time window restates at its opening rate'); 1dc1c0f only removed the throw sentence. The premise holds: a time-tiered pass straddling a boundary repriced confidently at one rate, contradicting another comment's 'range' promise. The agent's span sampling over axis breakpoints correctly handles off-peak-ends-peak-between, which the reviewer's from/to comparison would miss.
guidance_note: When a record keeps an interval but the pricer reads only one end, either price the interval or state the approximation in the output; don't leave a comment that promises a range.

narrative: Each round raised one finding. The F1 basis-dispatch fix was the right structure, but it left a stale 'write-side-only' comment (F2) and an arm that discarded a known subscription figure (F3), costing two rounds. F4 and F5 were independent original-PR gaps in restatedFromTable's handling of the recorded instant. The PR hit the round cap, and the final span-pricing commit e6cc4eb went unreviewed.
guidance_observations: The original restatedCost design had three latent holes in one 6-line function: no basis dispatch, an unscreened from, and from-only pricing. Each surfaced in its own round, so enumerating the record's fields and variants up front would have collapsed rounds 0, 3 and 4.
The largest structural change (e6cc4eb, span sampling) landed after the round cap and merged with no review at all; a change of that size warranted another review.

evidence: The summary step is `if: always()`, and its fallback pointed at 'Gate the candidate', which never runs under the always-failing refusal step. The agent took the reviewer's first option (fix the message), made it step-agnostic, and declined the moratorium branch, a defensible call since it would duplicate the moratorium fact.
guidance_note: When inserting an always-failing step at the top of a job, read every `if: always()` step below it for messages that assume a later step ran.

evidence: `[`zai-eval-harness-5ux`]` has no URL or reference definition, so it renders with literal brackets, while the rest of the file cites tickets as bare backticks.
guidance_note: When citing a local ticket in markdown, use the file's existing citation style rather than link syntax with no target.

evidence: The diff deleted the job's `if:` but left the comment describing it in present tense ('Dispatch always runs... A PR runs only when...'). The agent deleted it, which was one of the reviewer's two options, and swept the header for the same drift.
guidance_note: When deleting a config key, delete or rewrite the comment block that documents it in the same hunk.

narrative: This small moratorium PR drew three independent round-0 findings, all real and all leftovers of removing the trigger and the job `if:`. All were fixed in one commit, and round 1 approved. The agent's F1 split (take the message fix, decline a mode branch) was the right call.
guidance_observations: All three findings were drift left by deletions: a removed `if:`, a removed trigger, and a newly inserted failing step. One sweep of every comment and message that referenced the removed mechanism would have produced an approve-on-first-round PR.

evidence: A status-check re-run plans no jobs, so `done` is [] and the single suite-timing.json was overwritten with an empty suite on the normal resume path. The agent was right that skip-when-empty still loses data on a partial resumed leg. Per-invocation files plus a reducer fix both cases.
guidance_note: When adding a durable artifact to a command whose resume is 'run it again', write per-invocation files from the start, matching the append-only run-dir pattern the command already uses.

evidence: USAGE listed `findings.json, summary.txt, usage.json, transcripts/` while writeRunRecord now also writes schedule.json; 3f188c0 updated USAGE and the README artifact list.
guidance_note: When adding an output file, grep for an existing sibling filename (e.g. usage.json) and add the new one wherever the list appears.

evidence: The JSON.stringify(undefined) + '\n' path does write literal 'undefined'. Throwing at a write seam covering every field is better than `?? null`, which would hide a broken producer. The sweep missed summary.txt, though (see F6).
guidance_note: When generalizing a guard to 'every field' of a writer, list the writer's lines and route each one, text writes included, before claiming 'every'.

evidence: The fixture used `{ tag: { phase }, span }` and asserted `spanMs(s.span)`, while a live replay's schedule.json (pasted in the reply) has phase at top level and the span at usage.span. The fixture also lacked sweepCap/scopeCount, which scheduleRecord requires.
guidance_note: Build test fixtures for a produced artifact through the producer's own constructors (scheduleRecord/spawnRecord) instead of hand-writing the shape.

evidence: No test drove main()'s timing write or its warn-and-continue catch, though every other main() wiring in the file had a spawnSync test. As the agent noted, that gap is what let the F1 clobber through. 3f188c0 added three CLI tests, including the re-invocation regression.
guidance_note: When adding an effectful write in main() of a file whose other main() behaviors are covered by spawnSync tests, add one for the write and one for the re-invocation path in the same commit.

evidence: 3f188c0 routed meta/usage/schedule/findings through jsonBytes and justified it as 'every field', but left `fs.writeFileSync(..., summary + '\n')` unguarded. The agent conceded its own 'guarding one field leaves three' argument applied and added a shared `present` enforcer.
guidance_note: When a fix's justification is 'the same defect exists in N sibling lines', enumerate the lines in the reply and check each, rather than only the ones with the same expression shape.

evidence: The F1 fix's README text said '`readSuiteTiming()` folds the legs into one answer' as if it were a user-facing capability, but only tests call it. The agent softened the doc (the reviewer's second option), with sound reasons not to wire a loud reader into main().
guidance_note: When documenting a new helper, state who calls it; if the only caller is a test, say it is a library primitive with no reader yet.

evidence: readSuiteTiming, new in the F1 fix, catches only JSON.parse failures. A leg missing elapsedMs folds to NaN, and one missing replays splices undefined in via flatMap, despite the comment claiming any corrupt leg is loud. 0d15fb8 added shape checks.
guidance_note: When writing a reader over files on disk, parse to a proven shape (types of every field the fold uses) rather than only catching a syntax error, before claiming 'a corrupt X is loud'.

narrative: Round 0 raised five real findings. The agent took sound different fixes for the two structural ones (per-leg timing files, a write-seam guard). Round 1 consisted entirely of gaps in those fixes: the seam skipped summary.txt (F6), the README overclaimed the new reducer (F7), and the reducer validated syntax but not shape (F8). Round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent's different-fix choices were better than the reviewer's proposals both times, but each new mechanism shipped with a comment claim ('every field', 'a corrupt leg is LOUD', 'folds into one answer') broader than the code. Checking each such claim against the code before pushing would have saved round 1.
